newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday May 15.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi held long talks with Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio in a move that was harshly criticised by the centre-right opposition as political interference in the country's economy (all).

* Massimo D'Alema, leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) and president of the all-party parliamentary commission aimed at carrying out constitutional reforms, said he backed the idea of a prime minister chosen directly by the people as leader of the majority rather than that of a directly-elected president. Centre-left forces also would like to empower the prime minister to dissolve parliament in case of a vote of no-confidence against it (all)

* Enrico Giovannini, the chief economist of state statistics institute ISTAT, said Italy will see close to zero gross domestic product growth in the first quarter of 1997. Giovannini also said he saw some sign of optimism for GDP growth in the second quarter of the year. ISTAT also said Italy has made significant advances towards meeting the entry terms of the European single currency but it is facing a problem with unemployment and has to tackle welfare reform. ISTAT report also showed how the problem of unemployment affected mostly young people (all).
* Cement producer Fratelli Buzzi confirmed the group would launch a public buy offer (OPA) for Unicem shares (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* The latest report by Italian Banking Association (ABI) showed bankers expected to see only a limited upturn in consumer price inflation in the second half of this year while economic recovery would continue to be slow. ABI's report also showed deposits in the Italian banking system fell in April while loans rose only slightly (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
